blacklistabilityReview.evidence: On 2026-09-29, node.zano.org getinfo reported height 3837194, HF7 active, version 2.2.3.601[bfbe5c1-dirty-release_compact], and pre_hf_tx_freeze_period_active false. The adjacent get_asset_info read for 86143388bd056a8f0bab669f78f14873fac8e2dd8d57898cdb725a2d5e2e4f8f returned owner 497d6b7acd06401c59b2d52a3967968e8ca507a25f80e44d2bb4b5f8a348c7c1, empty owner_eth_pub_key, hidden_supply false and 12,000,000 fUSD supply. Latest published release 2.2.3.600 (98bbd725) validates the owner signature only for EMIT and UPDATE; ETH-signature ownership changes authentication, not holder permissions. Contrary to the update_asset documentation's owner-only description, validate_ado_update_allowed also permits metadata changes; UPDATE cannot change current supply, maximum supply, ticker, name, decimals or hidden-supply mode. PUBLIC_BURN requires the transaction's asset amount commitment and balance proofs, not an owner privilege to burn another holder's outputs. No issuer blacklist, pause, seizure or mutable transfer hook was identified. HF7 rolls the chain back to 3833000 and disables gateway input/output types by consensus. The September 2026 rollback was performed by Zano chain developers, not the fUSD issuer, unlike Zephyr where the issuer shipped the 2025 transfer-halting hardforks; it therefore does not establish an fUSD issuer-controlled holder restriction. The issuer FAQ confines fUSD to Zano and describes Ethereum/TRON routes as swaps into native fUSD, not deployed fUSD wrappers. The 2026-09-29 11:42:16 issuer dashboard discloses 1,328,148.90 ZANO worth $7,650,137.67 and 4,436,896 self-held fUSD; excluding own uncirculated tokens, disclosed collateral is 100% native ZANO and computed exposed reserve share is 0%. The FAQ separately identifies DAI swap-liquidity reserves without a balance or evidence that they collateralize circulating fUSD; this remains an unquantified liquidity-rail exposure, not evidence of majority reserve exposure. The rollback/security incident and swap-service interruption remain separate from direct issuer freeze authority.

oracleRisk.summary: Freedom Dollar uses a shared ZANO reserve and independent market-making bots. Its issuer-linked public bot source reads ZANO/USDT order books from MEXC and optionally CoinEx, aggregates orders and maintains WebSocket connections on a 30-second loop. The source trades existing wallet funds and does not issue tokens. A complete inventory of live bot versions, operators, pricing configurations and enforced stale-price or fallback behavior remains unverified, so the system-wide pricing tier remains opaque.

branchApplicability.rationale: FUSD has one shared ZANO reserve and no borrower-specific collateral positions or liquidation markets. Its market-making path values ZANO to place buy and sell orders near the dollar target. An issuer-linked implementation is now public and trades existing wallet funds without minting; the complete live operator and pricing configuration remains unverified. The disclosed price-sensitive mechanism is therefore reviewed at top level.
